basis: Complement C9 deficiency is an immunodeficiency; infection susceptibility does not establish damage to another organ.
Inflammation of the urinary bladder, most commonly caused by bacterial infection; noninfectious subtypes also exist.
Neurologic thermoregulatory disorder; episodic arrhythmia, sweating and gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish lasting organ damage.
Inherited susceptibility to glioma identifies the CNS as the target organ; susceptibility alone does not establish an existing tumour or other organ damage.
Disordered central planning of gait; the definition explicitly excludes motor weakness and sensory impairment.
Joubert brain malformation; nephronophthisis/end-stage kidney disease 6/7 and scoliosis 3/7. Ocular motor abnormalities are mainly neurologic; retinal damage frequency unspecified.
Paget carcinoma involves the epidermis of scrotal skin; its location does not make it a disease of the testis.
Immune-mediated arteritis damages the ocular circulation and causes defining ischemic optic nerve injury and vision loss.
Progressive myoclonic epilepsy with ataxia and cognitive deterioration; no common direct injury outside the nervous system is established.
Severe developmental brain disorder; fixed flexion contractures 2/3 support musculoskeletal involvement; exotropia 2/3 and optic disc pallor 1/3 support ocular involvement.
Lysosomal lipid storage disorder with defining adult-onset neurologic degeneration; common damaging hepatic or splenic dysfunction is not established for this subtype.
Neoplasm occupying or arising in the heart; no other organ is consistently damaged across this umbrella.
Drug-induced disorder of motor control; movements of skeletal muscles do not establish intrinsic muscle injury.
Inherited epidermal adhesion disorder causing acantholysis, blisters and erosions; despite its pemphigus synonym, it is not autoimmune.
Retinal degeneration and sensorineural hearing loss define the syndrome; mitochondrial inheritance alone does not establish a separate metabolic phenotype.
Pregnancy-related trophoblastic neoplasm arises in reproductive or placental tissue, outside the axes; metastatic organ damage is not universal or defining.
Stenosis of the cardiac aortic valve defines the disease.
Spinocerebellar and peripheral neurologic degeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy is frequent (30-79%). Ophthalmoplegia reflects neurologic motor dysfunction, not intrinsic eye injury.
Carcinoma originating in the uterus, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no other organ is commonly involved by definition.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dilatation in 5/5 patients and variable systolic dysfunction.
Squamous carcinoma of the bladder urachal region; the urinary bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Carcinoma arising from thyroid follicular cells; capsular or local vascular invasion does not establish a separate cardiovascular disease.
Mutilating palmoplantar and periorificial keratoderma; constriction bands are cutaneous. Digit autoamputation 1/6 and corneal opacity 5-29% fall below threshold.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology, motility and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other axis involvement is established.
Congenital neutropenia and monocytopenia cause immunodeficiency with recurrent bacterial infections; no specific additional organ injury is consistently established.
